title: Fluid card tiling and graceful canvas fallbacks for Console dashboards and modals
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a resilient, content-aware tiling system for dashboard cards and modal surfaces that preserves data density on narrow viewports and provides graceful fallbacks for canvas-based charts on legacy browsers. This ticket covers layout rules, reflow animations, chart fallback strategies, and cross-browser workarounds (Safari/older Edge) to minimize visual regressions across Redwood Console pages (cost views, rollouts, and multi-panel dashboards).
background: Multiple customer reports and internal observability dashboards showed layout breakage when panels are resized or when certain charts use canvas drawing on older Safari versions. Current behavior: abrupt breakpoints, clipped chart canvases inside modals, and inconsistent stacking order for floating panels. Engineering has prototyped a responsive grid but needs a design spec for prioritization, animation, and fallback visuals.
design_goals: Create a deterministic card tiling algorithm for 1-3 columns that prioritizes key metrics and preserves affordances (action buttons, timestamps)
Define micro-interactions for reflow (enter/exit animations, placeholder shimmers) that feel snappy under a tight performance budget
Provide a non-canvas fallback for critical charts (sparklines, cost breakdowns) and a visual policy for degraded environments
Standardize modal stacking and overscroll behavior when charts resize or when the KV cache panel opens underneath
Deliver accessible keyboard and screen-reader friendly behaviors for collapsed/expanded card states
constraints: Keep repaint/reflow budget under 20ms for common viewport sizes (desktop and tablet)
Avoid introducing new network dependencies; fallbacks must render client-side
Must work without CSS container queries in older browsers — include feature detection and safe CSS-only fallback
Match existing Redwood visual language (typography, tokens) and keep token usage explicit for engineering handoff
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard pages render 1, 2, or 3 tile columns deterministically based on width breakpoints with no content overlap
When a viewport crosses breakpoint, tiles animate reflow using a 120ms ease-out transition and do not trigger visible layout thrash
Canvas charts degrade to SVG sparklines or simplified stacked bars when browser feature-detects missing WebGL/canvas-subpixel APIs
Modals maintain a max-height calc that prevents chart clipping; internal vertical scroll only activates inside modal content area
Keyboard users can expand/collapse dense cards and focus travels predictably; screen readers announce collapsed state and primary metric
Design spec includes visual tokens, CSS variables, and explicit measurements for engineering (margins, gutters, card min-width/min-height)
Prototype validated in Chrome, Firefox, Safari 14+, and Edge (Chromium and Legacy where available); cross-browser UI bugs logged and prioritized
tasks: Finalize tile priority rules and collapse thresholds (design)
Create Figma prototype with 3 responsive breakpoints and animation states
Produce an accessible interaction spec (keyboard flows + ARIA states)
Work with frontend to implement feature-detect flags and SVG fallback components
Run visual QA across target browsers and capture regression screenshots
Document perf budget and provide simple metrics dashboard for SRE to monitor reflow frequency
decisions: Use CSS grid for primary tiling with explicit minmax() constraints to avoid percentage rounding drift
Fallback charts will be shipped as simplified SVG components generated client-side to avoid extra network calls
Reflow animations will prioritize transform/opacity where possible; height transitions only used when necessary with double-buffering technique
Modal internal scrolling preferred over global body scroll when content height exceeds max modal height
review_comments: PM (Arjun Rao): Suggest we expose a per-dashboard toggle for 'dense mode' so power users can opt in — include in spec notes
Engineering (Liam O'Connor): Concerned about ResizeObserver polyfill size on older browsers; requested perf budget and optional lazy-init of observers
Accessibility (Priya Menon): Requested explicit aria-expanded on collapsed cards and announcement text for metric updates — added to interaction spec
Design review (Olivia Park): Animation duration feels long on low-powered devices; recommend conditional-reduced-motion handling
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with ENG, PM, and SRE. Agreed to limit animation to 120ms and to add a perf probe for reflow events.
2026-03-04: Initial Figma shipped. Included 1/2/3 col layouts and modal max-height proposals. Shared with frontend for early feedback.
2026-03-07: Engineering PR opened with CSS grid implementation and a basic SVG fallback for sparklines (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2134).
2026-03-09: Cross-browser QA notes: legacy Edge needed an explicit transform-style preserve-3d tweak; Safari 13 clipped canvas in nested scrolling contexts — SVG fallback confirmed workable.
2026-03-10: Submitted design for In Review. Requested pairing session with frontend engineer to finalize container query fallbacks.
